To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Ang2 plasma levels were significantly higher in AKI patients compared to controls.
the endothelial Ang/TIE2 system is in imbalance in patients who develop AKI.

Ang2 plasma levels are increased in patients that develop acute kidney injury after cardiac surgery compared with matched control patients, and that plasma Ang2 is positively correlated with urinary NAG, an AKI marker.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of angiopoietins in AKI after cardiac operations.
the role of the endothelium and the endothelial specific Ang/Tie2 pathway during AKI after cardiac bypass.
the pathophysiology of AKI after cardiac surgical intervention.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Ang/Tie2 dysbalance is associated with AKI after cardiac surgical assisted by cardiopulmonary bypass.
the Ang/Tie2 pathway is involved in AKI, and the Ang/Tie-2 system might be a potential therapeutic target in patients that develop acute kidney injury after cardiac surgery.
Ang/Tie2 is deranged in AKI, but the role of Ang2 in AKI is not clear.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Ang2 levels are increased, whereas Ang1 levels decrease over time in patients who develop AKI after surgery, and that this is accompanied by a positive correlation between Ang2 and NAG, a marker of tubular damage.
AKI is associated with a higher Ang2/Tie2 balance.
Ang2 levels increase and Tie2 levels decrease after cardiac surgery in patients that develop post-operative AKI.
The main takeaway from our work is that
AKI patients have higher Ang2 levels than controls.
the endothelial specific angiopoietin/Tief2 system is deranged after cardiac surgery.
Ang2 is a potential novel marker of AKI after cardiac surgical procedures, which may be used to identify patients at risk of developing AKI.
